title: Diatom polyamine emulsions grow capacitor silica molds without lithography
idea: Diatoms build frustule pores by letting phase-separated polyamine droplets template silica precipitation; spin a long-chain polyamine/phosphate film that breaks into droplets pinned on each hydrophilic storage-node landing pad, then feed silicic acid so silica grows only in the continuous phase. Burning out the organics leaves a self-registered honeycomb mold of deep pores for the cylinder capacitor.
why: Deletes the capacitor-mold exposure, its hardmask stack and the 60-75:1 plasma etch (facts 1, 4) with a room-temperature wet step; est. one fewer critical litho layer and 8-12% lower wafer cost.

title: Morpho-wing interference lithography prints the periodic cell array maskless
idea: Morpho scales make color by multilayer interference; the DRAM array is a perfect lattice, so expose active, buried-wordline and storage-node layers with 3- or 6-beam 193 nm immersion interference (~70 nm pitch hexagonal lattice, near-zero roughness), then one spacer doubling to ~35 nm. Array edges are trimmed and periphery printed afterwards with a cheap ArF mask.
why: Moves 3-4 of the 5-7 EUV array exposures onto a laser-and-optics bench costing ~1/20 of an EUV scanner (fact 4); est. 15-20% lower wafer cost and a large capex cut.

title: Phototropic resistless patterning: exposed surface sites switch on growth
idea: Shoots grow toward light; coat the wafer with a monolayer of photolabile-capped amines (nitroveratryl-type groups) that 193/248 nm light uncaps, and only uncapped sites nucleate ALD of the hardmask or metal. The pattern is grown directly, with no resist coat, bake, develop, strip or descum.
why: Removes ~6-8 steps and the track tool per patterned layer; est. 30-40% shorter litho-module cycle time and chemical use (fact 4).

title: Chromatophore-shrink mastering makes nanoimprint templates without e-beam writers
idea: Squid chromatophores expand and contract pigment sacs elastically; write nanoimprint master patterns at 4x size with cheap i-line lithography on a resist atop a biaxially pre-stretched shape-memory polymer, release it so the relief shrinks 4x, then electroform a nickel or replicate a quartz daughter. Shrink distortion is measured once and pre-compensated in the 4x layout.
why: E-beam NIL mastering costs ~$0.5-1M and weeks per layer; this targets <$20k and days, making nanoimprint viable for DRAM layers that now need EUV (fact 4).

title: Butterfly-scale gyroid electrodes grown inside lipid cubic-phase templates
idea: Butterfly scales grow gyroid networks from folded cell membranes; fill a shallow ~300 nm capacitor well with a monoolein lipid cubic phase (a self-forming gyroid with 5-10 nm water channels), electrodeposit Ru through the channels, wash out the lipid and ALD-coat the bicontinuous electrode with high-k and plate. Surface area per volume rises ~15-20x.
why: Reaches ~5 fF in a 4-5:1 well instead of a 60-75:1 pillar (fact 1), deleting the costliest high-AR etch and support layers; est. ~10% lower wafer cost and less etch-tool capex.

title: Nacre-style perovskite nanosheet tiling gives room-temperature k~200 dielectrics
idea: Nacre is brick-and-mortar layering; tile exfoliated Ca2Nb3O10 or Sr-niobate nanosheets (k 200+ at ~2 nm) by Langmuir-Blodgett or electrophoretic layer-by-layer deposition, with a one-molecule polycation 'mortar' between bricks, from water dispersions below 100 C in a dip tool.
why: k~200 vs ~40 for ZrO2 stacks roughly quadruples charge per area (fact 1, target k~70), cutting capacitor height ~3-4x; dip tools cost <1/10 of ALD clusters.

title: Sea-urchin amorphous precursor infiltration crystallizes high-k inside pores
idea: Sea urchins fill spine molds with a liquid-like amorphous carbonate and crystallize it in place; flow a polymer-stabilized liquid amorphous titanate precursor into capacitor holes by capillarity, then crystallize it to rutile TiO2 or SrTiO3 (k 80-150) at low temperature on a thin seed liner that templates the phase.
why: Delivers k~100 (fact 1) with a spin-and-bake instead of slow ALD supercycles; est. 5x faster dielectric module and a shorter, easier-to-etch capacitor.

title: Xylem transpiration draws metal nanoink void-free into deep capacitor holes
idea: Trees lift sap by evaporation through nanoporous leaf surfaces; cap the wafer with a nanoporous evaporation membrane so solvent leaves only through the top, pulling a Ru or Mo nanoparticle ink into 60:1 storage-node holes without trapped voids, then sinter at ~350 C.
why: Replaces CVD TiN/W electrode fill, removing tungsten (China ~80%) and costly CVD fill tools; wet-bench fill at est. 1/5 tool cost (fact 1, resources).

title: Magnetotactic self-registration aligns HBM dies without precision bonders
idea: Magnetotactic bacteria align magnetosome chains to a field; electroplate a coded pattern of CoFe nanomagnet dots on each die backside and a matching soft-magnetic pattern on the target, float dies on a thin fluid film in a uniform field so they snap into <200 nm registration, then bond the whole batch in one anneal.
why: Replaces serial thermo-compression and hybrid bonders (~$3-5M each, ~1k units/hour) with batch self-assembly for HBM stacks (fact 6); est. 10x stacking throughput and ~80% less bonding capex.

title: Bone-remodeling deposit-and-resorb supercycles self-align contacts without masks
idea: Bone is laid down and resorbed continuously, with net growth only where signals favor it; run ALD supercycles that deposit a dielectric everywhere and then a short etch that removes the thinner nuclei on metal but not the faster-grown film on oxide, repeated ~30x, so an isolation mask grows only on dielectric and contacts self-align.
why: Deletes 1-3 critical contact/via masks and their overlay budget (fact 4); est. 5-8% lower wafer cost.

title: Mitotic-spindle field assembly places pre-grown nanowire access transistors
idea: The spindle lines chromosomes up at the metaphase plate with fibers and forces; grow single-crystal Si or oxide-semiconductor nanowire transistors in bulk off-wafer, suspend them in a dielectric fluid and use AC electrode arrays to pull one into each cell site by dielectrophoresis, then bond and contact them.
why: Takes transistor making off the array wafer, removing ~10 front-end masks and high-temperature steps and letting arrays be built on cheap substrates; est. 30% fewer wafer process steps.

title: Clonal-selection redundancy lets cheaper, sloppier lithography make DRAM
idea: The immune system over-produces clones and keeps those that fit; design arrays with 15-20% spare rows/columns in fine 64-cell remap units, deliberately relax CD/overlay specs so 2-3 EUV layers move to ArF quad patterning at higher defect density, and let on-die test select working segments and burn the map into an antifuse bank.
why: Trades ~15% area for removing EUV layers and the tight defect spec; est. 15-25% lower wafer cost and ~10% lower cost per bit (fact 4).

title: Synaptic plasticity trimming tunes each access transistor after fabrication
idea: Synapses are wired roughly and then tuned by use; after fab, apply controlled field pulses that drift mobile hydrogen in the gate stack (or hot-carrier pulses) to raise each leaky transistor's threshold until its leakage passes a target, using the array's own sense amps as the meter.
why: Fixes the leakage tail post-fab (fact 3), cutting refresh 4-8x, and widens process windows so less inline metrology and rework is needed; est. 3-5% lower fab cost.

title: Electric-eel electrocyte stacks: shallow nanolaminate capacitors replace tall pillars
idea: Electric eels reach high output by stacking thousands of thin electrocytes; ALD-stack 8-12 alternating Ru/ZrO2 layers in a shallow ~150 nm recess and tie odd and even electrodes to node and plate through two self-aligned sidewall spacers, like a miniature multilayer ceramic capacitor.
why: Capacitor area multiplies by layer count without high-AR etching (fact 1); removes the 60:1 etch and support layers, est. 8-10% lower wafer cost and lower etch capex.

title: Honeycomb anodic alumina self-orders capacitor holes at extreme aspect
idea: Bees build hexagonal comb from local wall rules; sputter aluminum over the landing pads and anodize it, so pores self-organize into a hexagonal lattice whose pitch is set by voltage (25-60 nm) and whose sites are pinned by shallow DUV-printed dimples on the pads; pores grow 5-10 um deep in a wet bench, then get ALD electrode and dielectric.
why: Replaces the capacitor-hole exposure and hardest plasma etch (facts 1, 4) with a ~$100k anodization bench; aspect ratio becomes nearly free, removing the charge wall.

title: Quorum-sensing wafer test: dies self-test and broadcast only anomalies
idea: Bacteria act only when a population signal crosses threshold; every die runs built-in self-test at wafer level, powered through one blanket probe membrane, and reports only pass/fail and compressed fail maps over a shared optical or RF channel, so the tester becomes a power supply plus listener instead of a pin-heavy ATE.
why: DRAM test and burn-in is ~10-15% of cost; est. 5x less tester capital per wafer and 3x shorter test time.

title: Hermit-crab strategy: retrofit idle LCD panel fabs for oxide-TFT memory
idea: Hermit crabs move into empty shells; buy idle Gen-8.5 LCD/OLED backplane fabs (2.2 x 2.5 m glass, IGZO TFT lines installed) and run 2T0C gain-cell arrays at 1-2 um rules on glass (~30 GB per panel) for capacity-tier CXL memory, bonded to small CMOS controllers.
why: Panel-fab capex per square meter is ~1/30 of a DRAM fab and exists idle now, so capacity memory arrives in months rather than 3-5 years (fact 4); US-sited panel lines add domestic supply.

title: Stem-cell wafers: one front-end mask set, differentiated in last metals
idea: Stem cells differentiate on signal; run one universal array-plus-periphery front end for DDR5, LPDDR, HBM base and CXL parts, then personalize I/O, bank grouping and density bin in the last two metal layers by maskless e-beam or laser direct write.
why: Cuts mask sets across a product family ~4x (EUV sets cost $10-20M) and lets WIP swing between products within days; est. 10-15% better capex utilization.

title: Tardigrade dormant-wafer banks absorb DRAM demand and price swings
idea: Tardigrades suspend metabolism and revive on demand; run wafers through the capital-heavy front end (array and capacitor) during demand troughs, park them in dry-nitrogen 'cryptobiosis' stockers, and finish BEOL and test in 3-4 weeks when prices spike.
why: Keeps EUV front ends near 95% utilization across the cycle and halves response time to shortages (fact 4); effectively 10-20% more output per dollar of capex.

title: Elephant-ear vein chucks end helium backside cooling in fab tools
idea: Elephants shed heat through dense vein networks in thin ears; build electrostatic chucks with an embedded two-phase microchannel 'vein' network under a 0.5 mm ceramic face and a compliant nanostructured graphite contact layer, replacing helium backside gas in etch and deposition chambers.
why: Removes helium dependence (Qatar ~30% of supply offline) across dozens of etch/ALD tools per fab, a scarce-resource risk that can idle lines.

title: Rice-husk and diatomite biosilica makes Spruce-Pine-free quartz crucibles
idea: Plants and diatoms concentrate amorphous silica; acid-leach rice-husk ash or diatomite, chlorinate to volatilize metals, fuse to 5N+ synthetic silica and slip-cast Czochralski crucibles with a synthetic inner liner.
why: Breaks the >80% Spruce Pine high-purity quartz chokepoint using US rice-belt and diatomite feedstock in the hundreds of kt per year.

title: Termite-mound fab: sealed mini-environments plus passive stack-effect ventilation
idea: Termite mounds hold a steady climate with chimneys and earth thermal mass; build the fab as sealed tool mini-environments in an ISO 8 hall, pre-condition makeup air through buried earth tubes and exhaust it through solar-heated chimneys, eliminating most ballroom fan-filter units.
why: Cleanroom shell and HVAC are ~20-25% of fab construction and ~40% of facility power; est. 30% less shell capex and 40% less HVAC energy.

title: Blood-clotting repair: current-triggered electroless plating heals weak lines
idea: Platelets clot only at an injury; before final passivation, flood the wafer with an electroless Co or Ru bath and drive test current along every wordline and bitline so constrictions and thin spots heat locally, accelerating thermally activated plating exactly there until resistance normalizes.
why: Repairs near-open and high-resistance defects, a top yield killer at ~12 nm half-pitch; est. +3-6% yield, which also permits more aggressive, cheaper patterning.

title: Tree-ring shells: coaxial gain cell in every tier-hole crossing
idea: Etch one array of vertical holes through a 100-layer wordline/oxide stack, then grow concentric shells like annual rings: an outer IGZO write-channel ring, a metal storage ring cut into per-tier segments by a selective recess, and an inner read-channel 'heartwood' that the storage ring gates. Each hole-tier crossing becomes a capacitorless 2T0C cell.
why: One hole litho and etch serves all tiers, as in 3D NAND; at ~100 nm hole pitch and 100 tiers that is ~100 nm2 per bit, ~8-10x planar DRAM bits/mm2 at roughly flat wafer cost, with no capacitor (facts 1, 2).

title: Phyllotactic offset leaves halve the tier pitch of 3D DRAM
idea: Leaves alternate around a stem so they never shade each other; build the lateral 3D stack from two alternating SiGe compositions (A, B) and etch two interleaved hole sets, the first recessing only A tiers and the second only B tiers, so capacitor 'leaves' of neighbouring tiers sit half a cell offset rather than stacked. Coupling and leaning loads fall, so tier pitch can shrink from ~60 nm to ~30 nm.
why: Two masks serve every tier; doubling tiers per micron of stack lets an 80-tier stack fit where 40 did, reaching ~10x planar bits/mm2 at near-equal wafer cost (fact 2).

title: Snake-molt cleaving stacks forty single-crystal tiers from one donor
idea: A snake sheds a perfect thin copy of its skin each cycle; hydrogen-implant and cleave 30 nm single-crystal Si films from one reusable, repolished donor onto the growing stack with 20 nm oxide bonding interlayers, building 40 monocrystalline tiers, then pattern all tiers at once with one hole/slit etch and lateral recess.
why: Single-crystal lateral transistors fix the leakage tail that blocks 3D cells (facts 2, 3) with no Si/SiGe strain limit; 40 tiers patterned once give ~10x bits/mm2 while each tier adds only a bond/cleave/CMP cycle, keeping wafer cost near flat.

title: Coral strain-templating: each tier self-assembles directly atop the last
idea: New coral polyps settle on the old skeleton; use the vertical correlation seen in stacked quantum dots: tier N's buried metal nodes leave a periodic strain and surface-energy imprint through a ~10 nm spacer that pins the block-copolymer or nanoparticle self-assembly defining tier N+1's features exactly above them. Only the first tier is lithographed.
why: If replication fidelity holds, 12-16 tiers cost one critical litho plus a cheap coat/anneal per tier, ~10x bits/mm2 at near-planar wafer cost and no EUV beyond tier 1 (fact 4).

title: Cochlear ramp etch exposes every tier's contact in one step
idea: The cochlea maps frequency to position along a tapered duct; print a grayscale, thickness-tapered hardmask wedge once and ion-mill it together with the stack so the slope transfers into the tiers, opening each tier's wordline as a stripe at its own lateral position. One exposure and one etch replace the 30-100 resist-trim cycles of a staircase.
why: Staircases and tier contacts take ~15-20% of 3D memory cost and grow with tier count; a one-shot ramp flattens that, so 150+ tier DRAM (~10x bits/mm2) keeps near-planar contact cost (fact 2).

title: Bacterial S-layer protein crystals pattern the array at 9 nm
idea: Many bacteria coat themselves in S-layers, 2D protein crystals that recrystallize on surfaces in minutes; engineer a square-lattice S-layer (~9 nm period) with a metal-binding loop, recrystallize it over the array region guided by DUV-printed edge anchors, mineralize the pores into a Pt/Al2O3 hardmask and etch one vertical-channel gain cell per lattice site with self-aligned spacer wordlines.
why: ~80 nm2 per cell vs ~860 nm2 for 6F2 at F=12 nm gives ~10x bits/mm2 with no EUV in the array; the protein costs cents per wafer, so wafer cost stays flat (fact 4).

title: Spider-spinneret thermal drawing shrinks a macro preform into nanocell arrays
idea: Spiders draw nanoscale fibers from a gland; assemble a centimetre-scale preform of chalcogenide-glass channel, low-melting metal electrodes and polymer dielectric in the exact cell pattern, thermally draw it ~10^4x like optical fiber to ~20 nm features, then bundle, fuse and slice the fibers crosswise into thin 'memory wafers' that are hybrid-bonded onto CMOS.
why: Feature size comes from draw ratio, not lithography; one cheap preform yields kilometres of fiber, so slices can reach ~10x bits/mm2 at bulk-material cost with zero masks (fact 4).

title: Fiddlehead roll-up: printed foil memory coiled a hundred turns
idea: Ferns pack a large frond into a tight coil; roll-to-roll imprint a 2T0C oxide-TFT memory array on 2 um polyimide foil at ~1 um rules (processing cost per m2 ~1/100 of a silicon wafer), route bus lines to one edge, then wind the foil 100+ turns into a dense cylinder whose edge contacts bond to a CMOS controller.
why: Low planar density is offset by 100x volumetric stacking: ~10x bits per board footprint at equal or lower cost per bit, using printing lines instead of EUV fabs (fact 4).

title: Shipworm catalytic drilling replaces plasma etch for 200-tier holes
idea: Shipworms bore by chemistry rather than force; place Au or Pt catalyst discs, defined by the single hole lithography, on top of a 200-tier Si/SiGe stack and run metal-assisted chemical etching in HF/H2O2 so each disc sinks straight down, drilling ~30 nm holes at >500:1 aspect in a wet bench.
why: High-AR hole etch is the most capital-intensive 3D step and caps tier count; a MACE bench costs ~1/20 of a cryogenic etcher and goes deeper, so 150-200 tiers (~10x+ bits/mm2) arrive at about flat wafer cost (fact 2).

title: Brain-fold gyrification: build cells on deep corrugated wafer sidewalls
idea: The cortex triples its area by folding; etch the wafer once into 1.2 um tall fins at 120 nm pitch (ArF plus spacer doubling), then build cells on both sidewalls using only conformal ALD and horizontal bands defined by repeated deposit-fill-recess cycles, so every band along the fin height is a row of cells.
why: Sidewall area is ~20x the footprint; even at half the planar cell efficiency that is ~10x bits/mm2, with the extra area coming from cheap deposition/recess cycles rather than EUV (fact 4).

title: Synaptic-vesicle quantal storage: count charged ferritin dots per cell
idea: Synapses signal in discrete vesicle quanta; dip-coat 15 ferritin-derived 7 nm oxide cores as separate islands over a 1.5 nm tunnel oxide on each oxide-semiconductor channel, charge 0-15 islands by direct tunnelling (ns writes, high endurance, ~100 ms retention, refreshed like DRAM) and read the step-quantized channel current as 4 bits.
why: 4 bits per cell in a capacitorless cell about 2.5x smaller than 6F2 gives ~10x bits/mm2; the dots self-assemble in a dip step, so wafer cost is nearly unchanged (facts 1, 4).

title: DNA-brick 3D crystals cast an entire multi-tier cell array
idea: Grow micron-thick 3D DNA-brick crystals (programmed voxel lattices at ~2.5 nm resolution) on the CMOS wafer from anchor pads, with designed voids forming the channel, wordline and bitline network of a 6-tier gain-cell array; infiltrate by sequential ALD (In2O3, HfO2, TiN/Ru) and burn out the DNA to leave a ceramic-metal cast.
why: All tiers are patterned at ~8 nm pitch by one self-assembly step and no masks; 6 tiers x ~2x lateral shrink is ~10x+ bits/mm2, at flat cost if enzymatic DNA synthesis reaches <$50 per wafer (fact 4).

title: Pollen-tube confined epitaxy grows monocrystalline channels in every tier
idea: A pollen tube grows only inside the style's channel; deposit a cheap 120-pair PECVD oxide/nitride stack as in 3D NAND, strip the nitride through slits to leave tunnels, then grow single-crystal Si into all tunnels at once by template-confined lateral epitaxy seeded from the substrate at each slit base.
why: Replaces slow, strain-limited Si/SiGe epitaxial superlattices (capped near 30-60 layers) with 3D-NAND-cost stacks, making 120 tiers (~10x bits/mm2) affordable at near-flat wafer cost (fact 2).

title: Apical-meristem nanowires grow stacked transistors along their own axis
idea: Shoots add segments at the tip; grow vertical Si nanowires by catalyst-tip (VLS) growth from the pad lattice while switching dopant and Ge gases every ~25 nm, so each wire holds 16 axial n+/p/n+ transistor segments, then fill around the forest with alternating spin-on dielectric and conductor layers that become wordline tiers timed to the segments.
why: Channels for all 16 tiers come from one growth run instead of patterning; at ~40 nm wire pitch that is ~100 nm2 per bit, ~8-10x bits/mm2 at roughly flat cost (fact 2).

title: Pinecone hinges self-fold a planar array into ten stacked panels
idea: Pinecone scales fold by bilayer differential swelling; build a planar thin-film memory array on a released 1 um membrane with stress-engineered SiN/metal hinge strips between panels, then release it so the panels accordion-fold (Miura pattern) into a 10-high stack, with hinge lines carrying the bus wires to a base contact row.
why: Footprint density rises ~10x while cost per bit equals the planar process (folding is one release etch), so 10x density at the same cost per bit where package area is the limit (fact 6).

title: Thylakoid grana: atom-thin 2D channel tiers stacked at 10 nm
idea: Chloroplasts stack thylakoid membranes into dense grana; alternate low-temperature MOCVD MoS2 monolayers with ~8 nm ALD insulator to build a 60-tier stack only ~0.6 um tall, then form vertical wordlines and bitlines once through it so each tier is a lateral gain-cell layer with a 0.7 nm channel and almost no off-state leakage.
why: A 10 nm tier pitch (vs ~50-60 nm for Si/SiGe) puts 60 tiers in the height of 10, so one shallow hole etch yields ~10x bits/mm2 at near-flat cost and low refresh (facts 2, 3).

title: Mitochondrial cristae ribs fold lateral capacitors into short 3D cells
idea: Cristae multiply membrane area by inward folds; build each lateral capacitor tier from a mini-superlattice of three SiGe sub-layers with different Ge content, so the single lateral wet recess carves a rib-and-groove cavity and the electrode/dielectric deposited into it gains ~3x area per unit length.
why: Each capacitor leaf can be ~3x shorter for the same Cs (fact 1), shrinking cell pitch in every tier; a 40-tier stack then reaches ~10x planar bits/mm2 at near-flat cost because the ribs come from deposition, not lithography.

title: Exoskeleton-molt imprint tiers: nanoimprint each monolithic memory tier cheaply
idea: Arthropods form each new cuticle against the old one; build 10 monolithic oxide-semiconductor 2T0C tiers above CMOS and pattern each tier's critical layers by jet-and-flash nanoimprint from one shared master set replicated into daughters, at ~1/8 the per-layer cost of an EUV exposure and with no scanner.
why: Ten tiers at ~1/10 the litho cost each keep total wafer cost near one EUV-patterned planar array while reaching ~10x bits/mm2 (fact 4).

title: Cuttlebone chambers: air-gap tiers on pillars cut coupling and height
idea: Cuttlebone is thin floors separated by gas-filled chambers and tiny pillars; after the tier stack is patterned, dissolve sacrificial carbon or SiGe isolation layers through the slits, leaving air gaps (k=1) held by self-aligned oxide pillars at the bitline holes, then pinch-off seal the slits.
why: Air gaps cut inter-tier coupling ~4x so isolation shrinks from ~30 nm to ~8 nm, about doubling tiers per stack height; with a 50-tier-class process that is ~10x bits/mm2 for one extra wet etch (fact 2).

title: Myelin multilamellar self-assembly lays down twenty tiers in one coat
idea: Schwann cells wrap axons in dozens of uniform lamellae; spin a high-chi lamellar block copolymer that orders parallel to the substrate into 20+ layers (~12 nm period), then use sequential infiltration synthesis to turn one block into AlOx insulator and the other into In2O3 channel, creating a whole tier stack in one coat-anneal-infiltrate sequence below 200 C.
why: Tier-stack cost drops from ~100 depositions to one coat plus a few infiltration cycles; 40+ BEOL-compatible tiers with a single hole/slit patterning give ~10x bits/mm2 at near-flat cost (facts 2, 4).

title: Clam growth-line oscillating bath deposits the whole tier superlattice nonstop
idea: Clam shells lay periodic growth bands from a self-oscillating cycle; engineer the spontaneous potential oscillations known in Cu/Cu2O electrodeposition so a single bath alternates metal wordline layers and oxide-semiconductor layers ~15 nm thick, forming 100 tier pairs in one run with no valve switching, vacuum or tool transfer.
why: Tier-stack deposition at wet-bench cost and tungsten-free; 100 tiers patterned once give ~10x bits/mm2 at near-flat wafer cost (facts 2, 4, resources).

title: Neural pruning: over-grown random nanowire mesh carved into addressable cells
idea: Brains over-wire and then prune; solution-grow a dense random mesh of ~10 nm oxide-semiconductor nanowires between two orthogonal coarse electrode grids, then use electroforming pulses to burn out shorts and weak paths, characterize the surviving junctions on-die and address them through a learned map stored in a small SRAM table.
why: Self-assembled junctions far denser than the coarse lithographed grids give ~10x bits/mm2 using only relaxed ArF masks, if surviving-junction yield stays above ~30% (fact 4).

title: Octopus arm ganglia: in-tier decoders built in the same channel film
idea: Octopus arms carry their own ganglia; in a 3D stack, form a small oxide-TFT decoder in each tier from the same channel film and the same slit/hole patterning as the cells, so each tier needs only ~log2(N) shared address lines instead of N individually contacted wordlines.
why: Per-tier contacts, staircases and CMOS drivers stop growing with tier count, so 120+ tiers (~10x bits/mm2) can be built without the periphery (49% of the die) and contact cost scaling up (facts 2, 7).
